properties.description: crates/reflow2-core/tests/reply_budget.rs (10 cases) plus three checks in tools/smoke_mcp.py driving the built binary over real stdio, and one regression case in tools/test_reflow2_check.py. What it pins: an answer that fits comes back whole with no note; an answer that does not drops the cheapest information first (affected_ids capped, then the prose from EVERY row, never from some); `count` and `by_source` cover every open gap in every tier; the last resort — where a gap is genuinely absent from the list — says how many and keeps the highest-severity ones; a budget smaller than the empty reply does not underflow; a compacted row deserializes as a GapCandidate and asks the SAME question as the full one, because gap_to_prompt fills it back in from the graph; and a scoped answer is budgeted too, with different advice, because telling a reader who scoped to scope is advice they cannot follow. THE GATE CASE IS THE ONE THAT NEARLY GOT AWAY: reflow2_check.py judged a gap anchored by affected_ids, so a budgeted reply would have turned the build GREEN on 100 open critical gaps. Verified live by reverting the fix and watching the test fail.
properties.findings: 10 core cases, 3 smoke checks over real stdio, 1 gate regression case — all passing. MEASURED EFFECT on this design (77 open gaps, 2,920 nodes): the unscoped reply fell from 157,785 bytes on the wire to 53,181, a 66% cut, and `count` stayed 77. TWO DEFECTS CAUGHT BY THE TESTS RATHER THAN BY REVIEW. (1) reflow2_check.py judged a gap ANCHORED by `affected_ids` being non-empty; against a budgeted reply it printed 'OK — design and build agree (103 notes)' on 100 open critical gaps. Proven live by reverting the fix. (2) A budget of 0 reached the last-resort truncation with an empty list and underflowed `len() - lo`; `[]` still costs 2 characters, so the guard cannot be inferred from 'nothing to drop'. Also proven live by removing the guard and watching it panic. Both tests were checked for being INERT before being believed.
properties.name: detect_gaps answers within a budget, and a shorter answer is never a quieter one
